title: Reliable clonal seed reproduction across major crop families

concept.text: The innovation is a transferable way for crop plants to produce seeds that preserve the parent plant’s genetic combination. Through engineered apomixis, a desirable hybrid could reproduce through seed without the genetic reshuffling and segregation that normally occur during sexual reproduction. A substantial demonstration has been reported in rice; the broader concept is reliable operation across diverse crop families.

The reproductive system must coordinate three capabilities: forming an egg that retains the parent’s chromosome complement without recombination, initiating embryo development without fertilization of that egg, and completing compatible seed development. These processes must work together while maintaining seed production and keeping nonclonal offspring rare. The intended product is therefore a fertile seed-propagation system, rather than embryo formation alone.

significance.text: Reliable apomixis could preserve valuable hybrid genetic combinations through successive seed generations. Ordinary sexual reproduction can separate those combinations; clonal seed production could retain them, potentially preserving hybrid vigor and other useful combinations already assembled by breeding. The reported rice mechanism and genetic testing provide an experimental basis for that possibility, although they do not establish transferability across crop families.

Conditional downstream possibilities include simpler multiplication of selected hybrids, reduced dependence on repeatedly reconstructing the same hybrid cross, and wider access to desirable planting material. These are prospective consequences, not economic outcomes measured by the supplied study. Whether seed becomes cheaper or more accessible would also depend on production costs, licensing, distribution, seed quality and local farming practices.

As a practical synthesis, preserving a genotype does not guarantee that its performance will remain superior in every environment. Clonal propagation would preserve an existing genetic combination; it would not itself create drought tolerance, disease resistance or higher yield. Its agricultural value would depend on the genotype being propagated and on reliable performance under the conditions where the seed is used.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability within the proposed scope is a reproductive engineering system that transfers reliably among diverse crops while combining high clonality with ordinary fertility. The rice work addresses a major historical obstacle: engineered apomixis can produce clonal offspring yet still suffer from low reproductive frequency or poor seed production. Success requires both properties in the same plants.

The concrete biological challenge is coordinating altered gamete formation, parthenogenetic embryo initiation and successful seed development. Incomplete coordination can leave a mixture of reproductive outcomes or reduce the number of usable seeds. Measuring chromosome number helps identify those outcomes, but chromosome number alone cannot establish that offspring preserve the parental genotype; genetic comparisons are also needed.

For the broader platform, proposed engineering priorities are to establish which components require crop-specific adaptation, maintain reproductive performance over generations, and identify conditions that increase nonclonal offspring or reduce fertility. These are requirements inferred from the intended multi-crop capability. The supplied evidence does not establish how much redesign would be necessary in each crop family.

current_state.text: Song and colleagues reported a substantial rice demonstration in “Engineering high-frequency apomixis with normal seed production in hybrid rice,” dated 26 November 2024, DOI 10.1016/j.isci.2024.111479. Using an improved apomixis-inducing vector termed MiMe-ECA1-AZP2, selected engineered hybrid rice lines were reported to produce 95.0–100.0% clonal progeny with normal or nearly normal fertility, including seed-setting rates up to 89.7%. These results concern selected rice lines, rather than every engineered hybrid or multiple crop families.

The measurement distinction matters. The study used diploid progeny frequency as its measure of apomictic reproduction and supported genotype preservation with marker testing and whole-genome sequencing of sampled offspring. Two YY4949 lines produced 95.7–97.5% diploid progeny and had seed-setting rates statistically comparable to the wild-type control. Statistical comparability does not establish identical fertility, and the high diploid frequencies should not be read as whole-genome confirmation of every offspring.

The main article reports stable diploid frequencies and fertility from T1 through T3, with marker and sequencing results supporting preservation of the hybrid genotype in sampled progeny. Agronomic traits were assessed in a paddy field at Yuanyang in Henan province, China; fertility analysis examined all spikelets on three to eight randomly selected plants of each material. This provides multigeneration and field-based evidence within the reported experimental scope, rather than broad validation across production regions or environments.

The supplied review had access to saved, untruncated main article text, superseding the earlier account that full-text inspection remained blocked by a CAPTCHA. Its inspection did not include figure images, linked supplementary files or raw data, so those materials have not been independently assessed here. The supplied freshness search record is empty: it does not establish whether a transferable multi-crop platform remained unachieved as of 1 November 2026. That gap limits claims about the latest state of the field without undermining the dated 2024 rice report.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independently reproduce high-frequency clonal seed production with fertility comparable to appropriate controls in diverse crops, including at least a major dicot and a cereal. That pairing would demonstrate transfer beyond rice and across a substantial biological divide, but it would remain an initial breadth test. A claim covering major crop families would require evidence from additional representative families and relevant genetic backgrounds.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduce high-frequency clonal seeds with comparable fertility across crop families

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification should follow several generations and combine chromosome-number measurements with parent–offspring genotype comparisons. It should report the frequency and nature of departures from clonality, sampling sizes, uncertainty and seed-setting performance. The protocol should define acceptable clonality, fertility and sampling precision before testing; these would be proposed operational thresholds, not established standards supplied by the rice paper.
completion_criteria.label: Verify multigenerational clonality against predefined thresholds and report departures

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical validation should compare engineered lines with appropriate controls under field conditions, measuring seed production, germination, offspring performance and retention of the traits that motivated propagation. Independent teams should be able to reproduce the results using sufficiently documented methods and accessible validation data. Claims should state the crops, generations, environments and operating conditions tested. Finite demonstrations establish demonstrated breadth and reliability within those boundaries, rather than literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduce field performance and state tested operating limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BOT-04, “An inexpensive, broadly transferable method to edit and regenerate plants,” could help deliver reproductive engineering into more crops, while BOT-03, “Whole-plant synthetic genome construction and rewriting,” concerns a broader capacity to construct or revise genomes. BOT-06 concerns how an established genotype is reproduced through seed; editing, regeneration or genome construction alone does not establish clonal seed reproduction.

Roster-based synthesis: BOT-05, “Predictive plant biology from genome to whole-organism performance,” could help anticipate reproductive and agronomic consequences. BOT-12, concerning plant-wide communication and plasmodesmatal control, and BOT-17, concerning cell-division planes and tissue patterning, overlap with the developmental coordination involved in successful reproduction. BOT-13 concerns cell-wall growth and mechanical sensing. These concepts address explanatory or control capabilities distinct from a demonstrated apomictic seed system.

Roster-based synthesis: BOT-14, “Programmable, multigenerational epigenetic inheritance of adaptive plant traits,” also concerns inheritance across generations, but its central target is inherited epigenetic state. BOT-06 targets preservation of a genetic combination through clonal seed reproduction. BOT-09, concerning affordable preservation and recovery of exceptional plant diversity, shares a propagation and conservation interest; multiplying selected genotypes would not by itself preserve the breadth of plant diversity.

Roster-based synthesis: BOT-01, nitrogen-fixing cereal partnerships; BOT-02, a carbon-concentrating photosynthetic system in rice; BOT-07, transferable desiccation tolerance; BOT-08, durable immunity; BOT-10, durable additional soil carbon; BOT-15, perennial grain production; and BOT-16, control of plant–mycorrhizal nutrient exchange, concern distinct crop traits or ecological functions. Apomixis could potentially propagate valuable genetic combinations contributing to such traits, but would not establish the traits or guarantee persistence of their environmental and microbial interactions.

Roster-based synthesis: BOT-11 seeks a testable causal explanation for the early radiation of flowering plants. It shares an interest in plant reproduction and evolution, while BOT-06 is an engineering objective for contemporary crop propagation. Neither accomplishment would constitute completion of the other.

unresolved_issues: The supplied materials do not establish whether later work had demonstrated a transferable multi-crop platform by 1 November 2026.
Figure images, supplementary tables and raw data were not independently inspected in the supplied review.
The necessary crop-specific adaptations and achievable reliability across major crop families remain unestablished by the supplied rice evidence.
Operational thresholds for clonality, acceptable fertility, escape rates and sampling precision still need to be defined for a proposed validation program.
Broad environmental reproducibility, commercial seed-production performance and economic or access benefits are not established by the supplied evidence.

brief.title: Seeds that keep a crop’s winning genetic combination
possible: Farmers could grow successive generations of a chosen hybrid while keeping its genetic combination intact. Across major crop families, seeds would reliably produce genetic copies of the parent without sacrificing normal seed production.
why: Ordinary reproduction reshuffles a hybrid’s genes, separating combinations that breeders worked to assemble. Preserving those combinations could simplify seed multiplication and reduce the need to recreate the same hybrid cross for each generation.

sources.showed: Selected engineered hybrid rice lines produced more than 95% genetically copied offspring while maintaining normal or nearly normal seed production. Genetic tests supported preservation of the parent’s genetic combination in sampled offspring.
sources.quote: These synthetic apomicts maintained the agronomic traits of the elite hybrid rice.
sources.cited_for: Rice can combine frequent genetic copying through seeds with strong seed production.
sources.not_established: Success in selected rice lines does not establish reliable transfer across crop families.

sources.showed: Engineered Arabidopsis, a research plant, produced seeds that preserved the parent’s genetic combination without further crossing. Such offspring were rare, and seed production fell substantially.
sources.quote:
both diploid and tetraploid AtFix1
progenies completely inherited the hybrid genotypes of their
maternal parent across the entire genome
sources.cited_for: Genetic copying through seeds has been demonstrated beyond rice.
sources.not_established: The plants did not combine frequent production of unchanged offspring with normal seed production.

sources.showed: Engineered hybrid rice produced frequent genetic copies through seeds, with some lines approaching normal seed production. Seed production varied, and some lines showed unstable inheritance.
sources.quote:
Transmission of the high frequency of apomixis through skipped generations (atavism) was identified in two clonal 
lines, even though it remained stable in the majority of clonal lines.
sources.cited_for: Another rice study combined frequent genetic copying with near-normal fertility in selected lines.
sources.not_established: Performance was not consistently strong across lines or generations.

sources.showed: Following engineered rice across generations and locations revealed stable copying in most lines, declining copying in another, and location-dependent changes in others. Seed production remained below controls.
sources.quote: two apomictic lines exhibited alternating high and low induction rates when cultivated in different locations
sources.cited_for: Growing conditions and inheritance stability affect the reliability of genetic copying through seeds.
sources.not_established: The study did not establish dependable field performance or prove what caused the location-dependent changes.

shown: The strongest combination of genetic copying and seed production comes from selected rice lines studied by Song and colleagues. Their results persisted across generations and included field measurements. Chromosome counts tracked copying frequency; genetic tests checked sampled offspring.

Progress beyond rice remains less complete. Chen and colleagues demonstrated copying in Arabidopsis, but with rare unchanged offspring and poor seed production. Wang and colleagues’ rice results also show why reliability must be tested across growing conditions.
missing: A transferable system must combine frequent genetic copying with normal seed production across representative major crop families.
Repeated genetic comparisons must establish how often offspring depart from the parent’s genetic combination over generations.
Independent field trials must establish dependable seed production, germination and retention of the traits worth preserving.

milestones.label: Reliable seed copying across crop families
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce frequent seed copying with comparable fertility in a major broadleaf crop and a cereal. Additional families and genetic backgrounds would establish broader transfer.

milestones.label: Genetic copying stays reliable across generations
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to track chromosome counts, genetic identity, departures and seed production across generations against preset thresholds. Adequate sampling would establish how reliably the system preserves the parent.

milestones.label: Independent field trials establish performance and limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce seed production, germination and offspring traits in field trials using documented methods and accessible data. Stated growing conditions would define where the system works.

uncertain: How much redesign will different crop families need?
What rates of genetic copying, fertility and departures should count as reliable, and how much sampling would establish them?
Which environmental conditions disrupt copying, and can those effects be controlled?

page.title: Synthetic apomixis across crop families
page.definition: Engineered apomixis—seed reproduction that preserves the maternal genotype—operates in crops of Poaceae, Brassicaceae and Solanaceae. Hybrids retain their chromosome complement and agronomic traits through successive seed generations while maintaining seed production.

goal.need: Hybrid seed must be recreated each growing season because sexual descendants segregate genetically. The rice study published on 27 December 2022 described earlier engineered systems producing only 10–30% clonal seed. Apomixis addresses this recurrent crossing requirement by preserving hybrid genotypes through seed. Programmes now target its extension to millet, mustard and tomato.

completion.title: Hybrids in three crop families self-propagate clonally without reduced seed setting.
completion.criterion: In a hybrid crop from each tracked family, self-propagated seed produces >95% clonal offspring through successive generations, established by chromosome-complement measurements and genome-wide parent–offspring genotyping. Field-grown descendants retain the hybrid's agronomic traits and seed-setting rate relative to unmodified hybrid controls. Pollination for endosperm development is allowed. The >95% benchmark is adopted from rice research; it is not an external multi-family acceptance standard.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback, combining published crop targets and rice research benchmarks; no outside body was found to have defined this combined test.
completion.basis: Searches of research programmes, seed-certification standards and apomixis literature found no multi-family acceptance test or common fertility-equivalence margin. This fallback combines the >95% rice research benchmark with published requirements for self-propagation and field retention of hybrid traits. Family coverage follows the named millet, mustard and tomato programme targets; it does not establish transfer to every major crop family.

milestones.title: A plant produces functional gametes retaining its chromosome complement and unrecombined genotype.
milestones.criterion: A plant forms functional gametes retaining its chromosome complement and unrecombined genotype: the MiMe, or mitosis instead of meiosis, phenotype. On 9 June 2009, d'Erfurth et al. demonstrated this in Arabidopsis; crosses using male or female MiMe gametes produced triploids in 24/24 and 67/67 progeny, respectively. On 13 May 2024, Wang et al. reported MiMe in three hybrid tomato genotypes. These establish component function in Brassicaceae and Solanaceae; rice studies also use MiMe.
milestones.set_by: Plant reproductive genetics community: the MiMe phenotype defined by d'Erfurth et al. and subsequently applied in crop studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: The obtained plants produce functional diploid gametes that are genetically identical to their mother.

milestones.title: A plant produces clonal seed whose descendants repeat reproduction without a separate crossing partner.
milestones.criterion: A plant produces viable clonal seed without a separate crossing partner; descendants retain maternal ploidy and genotype and repeat the process. On 3 December 2024, Chen et al. reported 4 diploids among 105 Arabidopsis T2 seedlings, with three diploid progeny sequenced; T3 cohorts contained 3/66, 2/78 and 3/54 diploids. This is a Brassicaceae model plant. Rice also meets this stage. On 5 November 2025, Simon et al. reported two sorghum hybrids, including propagation through T4, with reduced seed production and germination. The cited tomato study establishes gametes, not this result.
milestones.set_by: Synthetic-apomixis research community: the self-propagation requirement stated by Chen et al., also applied in rice and sorghum demonstrations.
milestones.threshold_quote: engineered plants need to be self-propagating to produce clonal seeds.

milestones.title: Field-grown clonal seed descendants retain the source hybrid's agronomic traits and hybrid vigor.
milestones.criterion: Field-grown clonal descendants retain the source hybrid's agronomic traits and hybrid vigor. On 26 November 2024, Song et al. reported rice lines with 95.7–97.5% diploid offspring and 84.4–89.7% seed set, assessed in eight plants per material; two sequenced descendants retained genome-wide heterozygosity. The nonsignificant fertility comparison does not establish equivalence. On 9 February 2026, Wang et al. reported 0/56 diploid offspring in HW10's last tested generation and reduced seed set in different rice lines at Sanya and Changsha. The cited Brassicaceae and tomato studies do not establish this field result.
milestones.set_by: Synthetic-apomixis research community: Vernet et al., Discussion, proposed this field-validation criterion for rice; subsequent rice studies assess it.
milestones.threshold_quote: Trueness-to-type and hybrid vigor should ultimately be evaluated under a field trial to confirm greenhouse findings.

not_found: No regulator, seed standard, prize or research programme defining a multi-family apomixis acceptance test was found.
No shared fertility-equivalence margin, required generation count or prescribed field-testing design was found.
No published demonstration satisfying the combined completion test in Brassicaceae and Solanaceae was found.
The full text of the 2026 Brassica napus two-gene MiMe paper could not be opened.

results.finding: Rice line K6: two diploid plants from successive generations were genetically identical at 1,559,769 analyzed SNPs.
results.detail: The study reports stable diploid rates through T3. Genome-wide sequencing compared one T1 plant with one T2 plant.
results.quote: bioinformatic analysis of the sequencing data using 1 559 769 SNPs showed that the two plants were heterozygous at the whole genome and were genetically identical to each other

results.finding: Field-grown rice lines K6 and K7 produced 95.7%–97.5% diploid progeny; fertility was assessed in eight plants per material.
results.detail: The authors reported no apparent differences in measured agronomic traits and concluded that hybrid vigor was retained. The nonsignificant seed-setting comparison does not establish equivalence.
results.quote: The above results suggest that the hybrid vigor was fixed by the high-frequency apomixis in the fertility-normal apomictic hybrid rice.

results.finding: Self-pollinated Arabidopsis AtFix1 produced 4 diploid plants among 105 T2 seedlings.
results.detail: Whole-genome sequencing confirmed three diploid T2 progeny retained the maternal genotype. Three T2 lines produced diploid T3 progeny; seed set and clonal efficiency were reduced.
results.quote:
Of the
105 T 2 seedlings tested, 101 were tetraploid and 4 were diploid

results.finding: MiMe-only rice plants produced 61 tetraploid progeny.
results.detail: The authors attribute the tetraploids to fusion of diploid gametes, supporting functional unreduced gametes. The MiMe-only progeny were not genotyped to establish unrecombined gametes.
results.quote:
All progenies of the p24MiMe  T0 events were determined 
to be tetraploid (Table 1), a result of diploid gamete fusion.

results.finding: Five T1 clonal rice lines were genotyped; site similarity reached 98.92%.
results.detail: Diploid clonal plants produced further clonal descendants. Clonal-seed frequency remained above 90% in G23-6 through T2, although other lines showed generation-to-generation variation.
results.quote:
In contrast, clonal lines exhibited a site 
similarity of up to 98.92%, due to the absence of meiotic 
division.

results.finding: Four field-grown clonal rice lines were compared with the source hybrid.
results.detail: The lines resembled the hybrid in several traits, but some measured traits differed significantly. The text does not establish retention of hybrid vigor or yield.
results.quote:
Phenotypes were more thoroughly examined in  T1 progenies 
in four p94C transformants, grown with control wild-type.

results.finding: Hybrid rice line CL6 produced 36 diploid offspring among 44 tested.
results.detail: Descendants were propagated across generations, but ploidy was used as a proxy for clonality; the study does not report genome-wide parent–offspring genotyping.
results.quote: line CL6 initially exhibited a high clonal seeds rate (81.82%; 36/44)

results.finding: Field-grown HW10-T3 rice had 79.62% seed set, with 4 plants sampled per group.
results.detail: All lines in Sanya had significantly lower seed set than the wild-type control. The study reports morphological integrity but does not establish retention of the source hybrid’s agronomic traits and vigor.
results.quote: The highest rate occurred in the T3 generation of HW10 (79.62%), which showed a progressive increase across generations (60.84%→ 68.84% → 79.62%).

results.finding: Arabidopsis MiMe crosses produced triploid progeny in 24/24 male-gamete and 67/67 female-gamete crosses.
results.detail: Tested male and female gametes retained maternal heterozygosity at every genetic marker tested.
results.quote: The obtained plants produce functional diploid gametes that are genetically identical to their mother.

results.finding: Engineered Brassica napus produced over 95% viable clonal gametes; sample size not stated.
results.detail: Two genes were mutated in allotetraploid Brassica napus, fixing the genetic heterozygosity of F1 hybrids.
results.quote: Here, we demonstrate that mutating 2 genes in the allotetraploid oilseed crop Brassica napus effectively converts meiosis into a mitosis-like division, producing over 95% viable clonal gametes, and fixing the genetic heterozygosity of F1 hybrids.

results.finding: Rice OsMiMe plants produced functional diploid gametes; 50/50 selfed progeny were tetraploid.
results.detail: All 73 tested OsMiMe progeny retained heterozygosity at the 10 diagnostic markers tested on chromosomes 7 and 11, supporting clonal gamete production.
results.quote:
All the progeny (from two and three mother plants,
n
= 50 each) were tetraploid, indicating that both
Ososd1
and
OsMiMe
diploid plants produce diploid male and female gametes.

results.finding: MiMe produced unreduced, clonal gametes in three hybrid tomato genotypes.
results.detail: Sequencing of 12 tetraploid offspring found no crossovers; 3 showed local deviations indicating chromosome instability.
results.quote:
We bioengineered a 
‘mitosis instead of meiosis’ (MiMe) system that generates unreduced, clonal 
gametes in three hybrid tomato genotypes and used it to establish polyploid 
genome design.

results.finding: Hybrid rice: 673 of 679 progeny in one T2 line were diploid, corresponding to 99.1% clonal efficiency.
results.detail: Clonal reproduction persisted across generations; selected progeny retained parental heterozygosity by genome sequencing. Endosperm formation required fertilization, and large field populations were screened primarily by morphology.
results.quote: Among 679 and 766 progeny, we identified 673 and 760 diploid individuals, corresponding to clonal efficiencies of 99.1% and 99.2%, respectively.

results.finding: Field-grown Fix8_P2 rice descendants had 80.3% seed set; the number of plants assessed for seed set was not stated.
results.detail: The study reports comparable agronomic performance and seed set in field-grown descendants. However, it does not establish equivalence to the source hybrid through an equivalence test or directly demonstrate retained yield advantage over inbred parents.
results.quote:
Their overall agronomic performance and seed-setting rates (80.3 ± 2.9% and 75.8 ± 3.1%, respectively) remained indistinguishable from those of the control CY83 F
1
hybrid (78.3 ± 2.8%) (Fig. 4g, h).
